In detail

West Yorkshire Police recorded 820 crimes inside this ward's official boundary over the 3 months to July 2026 — 11.0 per 1,000 residents, the 13th highest rate of Leeds's 33 wards. The daytime score here is driven by shoplifting (25), burglary (16), vehicle crime (9); the evening/night score by violent crime (107), anti social behaviour (25), public order (19). Rated against the average of the city's own wards, never against another city.

Frequently asked questions

Is Cross Gates & Whinmoor safe?

Wandroz currently rates Cross Gates & Whinmoor in Leeds as roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Leeds, both by day and after dark. This rating is derived from West Yorkshire Police street-level crime records published at data.police.uk — an official statistic, not an assessment. High-footfall tourist, transit or shopping areas can read higher on this kind of measure without that meaning elevated risk per visit, since these statistics are normalised against registered residents rather than footfall — see the note on this page and the methodology page for the full caveats.

Is Cross Gates & Whinmoor safe at night?

At night, Cross Gates & Whinmoor is rated as roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Leeds. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Cross Gates & Whinmoor a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Cross Gates & Whinmoor's day rating (roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Leeds) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
